text: What is the defining virtue of finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation compared with frequency-domain solvers?
choices: It recovers the full transmission and reflection spectrum across the entire band from a single time-domain run
It solves each wavelength independently for higher accuracy
It is exact only for eigenmode (waveguide index) problems
explanation: Exciting with a short Gaussian pulse and accumulating a running DFT at flux monitors yields the whole spectrum in one run — the opposite of frequency-domain solvers, which repeat the solve at every wavelength. Choice 1 describes frequency-domain solvers; choice 2 is false (FDTD needs PML boundaries); choice 3 describes FEM's strength (mode solving), not FDTD.
